title: Compatibility with air / Positron
description: The Positron IDE seems to have removed support for {styler}, so if you want to use the IDEs formatting capabilities, you can't use {styler} (anymore). This raises the question (again) for compatibility between the two formatters. #1291 shows that once formatted with air, styler will hardly chance anything due to its non-invasiveness but initial diff is large. Hence, that means using format on save or other IDE features from positron is not conflicting in particular with the pre-commit hook for {styler}.

title: Formating of function arguments behaviour changes if `indent_by` is not `2`
description:
Problem: Changing `indent_by` configuration doesn't implement the same styling guides _(on "Double-indent")_

It changes the style to "Function-indent" ([reference](https://style.tidyverse.org/functions.html#long-lines-1))

Reproducible code:

``` r
foo_2 <- "foo <- function(
    bar) {
  NULL
}"

foo_4 <- "foo <- function(
        bar) {
    NULL
}"

styler::style_text(foo_2)
#> foo <- function(
#>     bar) {
#>   NULL
#> }
styler::style_text(foo_4, indent_by = 4L)
#> foo <- function(bar) {
#>     NULL
#> }
styler::style_text(foo_4, transformers = styler::tidyverse_style(indent_by = 4))
#> foo <- function(bar) {
#>     NULL
#> }

testthat::expect_identical(
    foo_2 |> 
        styler::style_text(indent_by = 2L) |> 
        as.character() |> 
        paste(collapse = "\n", sep = ""),
    foo_2
)

testthat::expect_identical(
    foo_4 |> 
        styler::style_text(indent_by = 4L) |> 
        as.character() |> 
        paste(collapse = "\n", sep = ""),
    foo_4
)
#> Error: paste(...) not identical to `foo_4`.
#> 1/1 mismatches
#> x[1]: "foo <- function(bar) {\n    NULL\n}"
#> y[1]: "foo <- function(\n        bar) {\n    NULL\n}"

# Sanity check using "tidyverse_style"

testthat::expect_identical(
    foo_2 |> 
        styler::style_text(transformers = styler::tidyverse_style(indent_by = 2L)) |> 
        as.character() |> 
        paste(collapse = "\n", sep = ""),
    foo_2
)

testthat::expect_identical(
    foo_4 |> 
        styler::style_text(transformers = styler::tidyverse_style(indent_by = 4)) |> 
        as.character() |> 
        paste(collapse = "\n", sep = ""),
    foo_4
)
#> Error: paste(...) not identical to `foo_4`.
#> 1/1 mismatches
#> x[1]: "foo <- function(bar) {\n    NULL\n}"
#> y[1]: "foo <- function(\n        bar) {\n    NULL\n}"
```

<sup>Created on 2024-02-14 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Aligning function parameters when a parameter has c()
description:
Dear developers and the community,

I generate the following function programmatically (please see the reprex below) and I wish to format it in a way that all parameters are aligned. Unfortunately, as you can see from the reprex the `arg3` and `arg4` are placed after the comma of the previous argument. I also provide the desired format.
Thank you so much for your time and help 🙏 

### Desired format
- option 1
```R
my_fun(
  arg1 = "val1",
  arg2 = "val2",
  arg3 = c(
    "val3",
    "val4"
  ),
  arg4 = c(
    "val5",
    "val6"
  )
)
```
- option 2
- interestingly in RStudio the CTRL+SHIFT+A makes this format and I am not sure whether it is using styler behind the scene. 
```R
my_fun(
  arg1 = "val1",
  arg2 = "val2",
  arg3 = c("val3", "val4"),
  arg4 = c("val5", "val6")
)
```


### Reprex
``` r
library(rlang)
library(styler)

args_l <- list(
  arg1 = "val1",
  arg2 = "val2",
  arg3 = c("val3", "val4"),
  arg4 = c("val5", "val6")
)

call1 <- rlang::call2(
  "my_fun",
  !!!args_l
)

txt <- rlang::expr_text(call1, width = 20)
styler::style_text(txt)
#> my_fun(
#>   arg1 = "val1",
#>   arg2 = "val2", arg3 = c(
#>     "val3",
#>     "val4"
#>   ), arg4 = c(
#>     "val5",
#>     "val6"
#>   )
#> )
```

title: compact trycatch
Unstable results for with certain styles
description:
# Background

I want to enforce consistent styling of a bioconductor package by running `styler` via github actions - after long long debugging I noticed that for certain files `styler` using the `biocthis::bioc_style` transformer transforms files back-and-forth between representations.

I don't know enough to understand if this behaviour is rather an issue with the `bioc_style` or `styler`.

# Description
I run into the issue that some transforms can be unstable, i.e. running the style command multiple times keeps switching the file between two states:

```
styler::cache_deactivate()
styler::style_file('varia.R', transformers=biocthis::bioc_style())
```
With `varia.R` being one of these two representations that are constantly switched by above command:
```
get_qc_measurements <- function(
  measurement_name,
  qc_pattern = "(blank)|(QCpool)|(QCmix)|(blank)"
) {
  grepl(qc_pattern, measurement_name)
}

```
and

```
get_qc_measurements <- function(
      measurement_name,
      qc_pattern = "(blank)|(QCpool)|(QCmix)|(blank)"
) {
    grepl(qc_pattern, measurement_name)
}

```

# Environment

R: 4.5.2
Packages: biocthis_1.17.4 styler_1.11.0  
```
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}

BiocManager::install("biocthis")
```

Thanks so much for this useful package!

# Dirty workaround

I found by running styler twice, it is possible to detect oscillating files - added this as a temporary workaround for cicd.

<details>

<summary>Code here</summary>

```
     - name: Check Bioconductor code style
        run: |
          library(styler)
          library(biocthis)
          
          # Disable caching to ensure consistent behavior
          styler::cache_deactivate()
          
          # Run styling twice to detect oscillations vs genuine issues
          cat("First styling pass...\n")
          styled1 <- styler::style_pkg(
            transformers = biocthis::bioc_style(),
            dry = "off"
          )
          
          cat("Second styling pass...\n")
          styled2 <- styler::style_pkg(
            transformers = biocthis::bioc_style(),
            dry = "off"
          )
          
          # Check for different outcomes between passes
          if (any(styled1$changed) != any(styled2$changed)) {
            cat("❌ Mixed results detected - genuine style issues found!\n")
            cat("First pass changed files:", any(styled1$changed), "\n")
            cat("Second pass changed files:", any(styled2$changed), "\n")
            
            if (any(styled1$changed)) {
              changed_files1 <- names(styled1$changed)[styled1$changed]
              cat("Files changed in first pass:\n")
              cat(paste("  📝", changed_files1), sep = "\n")
            }
            
            if (any(styled2$changed)) {
              changed_files2 <- names(styled2$changed)[styled2$changed]
              cat("Files changed in second pass:\n")
              cat(paste("  📝", changed_files2), sep = "\n")
            }
            
            quit(status = 1)
          } else if (any(styled1$changed) && any(styled2$changed)) {
            cat("⚠️  Styler oscillation detected - this is a known issue\n")
            cat("Files affected by oscillation:\n")
            oscillating_files <- names(styled1$changed)[styled1$changed]
            cat(paste("  🔄", oscillating_files), sep = "\n")
            cat("Accepting current state as valid due to oscillation bug.\n")
          } else if (any(styled1$changed)) {
            cat("❌ Bioconductor style issues found (stable after second pass)\n")
            changed_files <- names(styled1$changed)[styled1$changed]
            cat(paste("  📝", changed_files), sep = "\n")
            cat("\n\n💡 To fix style issues locally, run:\n")
            cat("Rscript scripts/style-bioc.R\n")
            quit(status = 1)
          } else {
            cat("✅ All R code follows Bioconductor style guidelines!\n")
          }
```
</details>
Caching prevents the oscillation locally. I also need to see next with other collaborators if this is viable or if it will switch for them.

title: [Question] Custom Styleguide Help
description:
Hi,

I'm working on trying to build out a custom style guide that's based upon the tidyverse style guide. I read through the vignette, but don't know that I understand what to do well enough to follow and adapt it for my own use case.

As I said, the style guide I'm trying to define in `{styler}` is really, at its core, implementing a few changes to the `tidyverse` style guide. The changes I'd like to implement are:

- Arguments across multiple lines separated by commas should have the comma at the start of the following line, not the end of the preceding line
- Code sections should have 5 blank lines between them, and the whole line should be 80 characters total
- Two blank lines should be at the end of the file

So, for example, this code:

```r

# Start section --------------------

ex_df = data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  y = letters[1:10],
  z = LETTERS[1:10]
)

# New section -------------------

ex_df |> writeRDS("~/Documents/ex_df.RDS")
```

should be reformatted as this code:

```r

# Start section ----------------------------------------------------------------

ex_df = data.frame(
  x = 1:10
  , y = letters[1:10]
  , z = LETTERS[1:10]
)





# New section ------------------------------------------------------------------

ex_df |> writeRDS("~/Documents/ex_df.RDS")



```

I follow in the vignette how to generate the AST and generally what the columns are intended to show, but I'm a bit lost with the rest of the implementation and how to define my own transforms for these few cases. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

title: Single-indent from Tidyverse style guide doesn't work
description:
According to the Tidyverse Style Guide https://style.tidyverse.org/functions.html#multi-line-function-definitions, functions should be either single-indent or hanging-indent.

**Single-indent doesn't seam to work properly with styler. The closing parenthesis is right after the last argument.**

Here is a simple reprex. (I made sure to deactivate and clear the cache of `styler` beforehand).
 

To help identify the problem, I also included a temporary workaround I have found where I deactivate two transformers that affect the indention and line breaks.
 

``` r
library(styler)
packageVersion("styler")
#> [1] '1.10.3'


cache_deactivate()
#> Deactivated cache.
cache_clear()
#> Nothing to clear. Cache directory is empty: /home/sagemaker-user/.cache/R/R.cache/styler/1.10.3

 
# single indention function example
single_indent_fun_decl <- "
foo <- function(
  arg1 = 3,
  arg2 = 5
) {
  arg1 + arg2
}
"

# Issue
transformers <- tidyverse_style()
style_text(single_indent_fun_decl, transformers = transformers)
#> foo <- function(
#>     arg1 = 3,
#>     arg2 = 5) {
#>   arg1 + arg2
#> }

# My current workaround
transformers <- tidyverse_style()
transformers$line_break$remove_line_breaks_in_fun_dec <- NULL # removing transformer
transformers$indention$unindent_fun_dec <- NULL # removing transformer
style_text(single_indent_fun_decl, transformers = transformers)
#> foo <- function(
#>   arg1 = 3,
#>   arg2 = 5
#> ) {
#>   arg1 + arg2
#> }
```

title: Don't force the first switch argument in-line with switch(
description:
I think we've hewed too closely to the style guide after #714:

```
library(styler)

styler::style_text('
switch(
  x,
  a = 1,
  b = 2,
  c = 3
)')
# switch(x,
#   a = 1,
#   b = 2,
#   c = 3
# )
```

Understand the `switch()` example in the style guide is like that, but I think _both_ having `x` on its own line _and_ moving it to `switch(x` are acceptable per the overall style guide, so `styler` shouldn't override valid syntax.

My reasoning is per: https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#long-lines

> As described under Named arguments, you can omit the argument names for very common arguments (i.e. for arguments that are used in almost every invocation of the function). Short unnamed arguments can also go on the same line as the function name, even if the whole function call spans multiple lines.

This becomes worse when the first argument is an expression, not just a symbol:

```
library(styler)

styler::style_text('
switch(
  tolower(x$switch_column),
  a = 1,
  b = 2,
  c = 3
)')
# switch(tolower(x$switch_column),
#   a = 1,
#   b = 2,
#   c = 3
# )
```

Here I think the original version is much clearer.

title: Regression of re-styling of unicode characters
description:
Hello,

I believe we are seeing a regression of https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/847 in R 4.4.0 on Linux. MacOS does not have this issue, and I haven't tested it on Windows.

## Steps to reproduce

### Start a shell using the rocker/verse:4.4.0 image

```shell
docker run -it --rm --platform=linux/amd64 rocker/verse:4.4.0 sh
```

### Observe the OS version

```shell
cat /etc/os-release
```

### Install styler from CRAN
```shell
R -s -e 'install.packages("styler", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org", quiet = T, Ncpus = 8)'
```

### Create a simple file containing unicode characters

```shell
echo 'a <- "R² μ ≥"' > ex.R
```

### Style the file

```shell
R -s -e 'styler::style_file("ex.R")'
```

### Observe the re-styled file

```shell
cat ex.R
```

Running `utils::getParseData(parse(text = 'suit <- "♠"'))` in the container gives me:

title: Disagreement with styler and lintr about long lines. Rstudio gives a better format
description:
Hi! 

I have this problem. Suppose you have this long line in your code:

```
value <- my_function(arg0 = 0, arg1 = 1, arg2 = 2, arg3 = 3, arg4 = 4, arg5 = 5, arg6 = 6, arg7 = 7)
```

Checking it with `styler`, returns the unmodified string. 
```r
styler::style_text("value <- my_function(arg0 = 0, arg1 = 1, arg2 = 2, arg3 = 3, arg4 = 4, arg5 = 5, arg6 = 6, arg7 = 7)")
value <- my_function(arg0 = 0, arg1 = 1, arg2 = 2, arg3 = 3, arg4 = 4, arg5 = 5, arg6 = 6, arg7 = 7)
```
However, `lintr` is complaining about the length of the line
```
[line_length_linter]: Lines should not be more than 80 characters. This line is 100 characters.	
```

In my opinion, Rstudio gives a better format: 
```r
value <-
  my_function(
    arg0 = 0,
    arg1 = 1,
    arg2 = 2,
    arg3 = 3,
    arg4 = 4,
    arg5 = 5,
    arg6 = 6,
    arg7 = 7
  )
```


What can I do to make `styler` behave like Rstudio in this case? 

Best.

title: Don't force line break for unnamed 1st argument
description:
I think the style guide is being mis- or over-interpreted here:

https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#long-lines

{styler} does the following:

```r
styler::style_text('
c(a,
  b
)
')
# c(
#   a,
#   b
# )

styler::style_text('
c(a,
  b = c
)
')
# c(a,
#   b = c
# )
```

It looks like {styler} has decided that unnamed arguments are _only_ allowed on the first line _if_ arguments on subsequent lines are named, but I don't see that explicated anywhere in the text.

{styler} is meant to be minimally-invasive, i.e. only make changes that are explicitly required by the style guide, hence I think this is a bug.

title: Indendation of low-precedence  infix operators
description:
Related to: https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/issues/1718

```r
y ~
  x1 +
    x2
```

Has parse tree `~(y, +(x1, x2))` so the `~` ends in line 3 and should thus cause an indentation for lines 2 and 3.
`+` ends in line 3 and should cause _another_ level of indentation on line 3.

``` r
styler::style_text("
y ~
  x1 +
    x2
")
#> y ~
#>   x1 +
#>   x2
```

title: Cannot Style Code When Script Is In Separate Window?
description:
Hi,

I'm surprised no one has asked about this, or if they have, then I apologize for missing it in my search through the issues.

In an R script, when I highlight and run the code below, _styler_ returns the lovely reformatted code. However, if I click the "Show in new window" button, _then_ highlight the code and run `styler:::style_selection()`, I receive the error `! No code selected`.

Is this inherent to the _styler_ package or am I missing some necessary step that must be taken when the script is in its own window?

```

  "please"
)
styler:::style_selection()
```

Thank you for your time!
Matthew

title: FR: Keep data.table chaining
description:
It is pretty canonical in `data.table` to write "query chains" like

```
DT[ , sum(x), by = .(a, b)
   ][ , median(V1), by = a]
```

But `styler` doesn't like these:

```
writeLines("
DT[ , sum(x), by = .(a, b)
   ][ , median(V1), by = a]
", tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".R"))
styler::style_file(tmp)

writeLines(readLines(tmp))
# DT[, sum(x), by = .(a, b)][, median(V1), by = a]
```

Would a rule to allow such chaining be in scope for `styler`?

title: Gaps in documentation for custom style guides
description:
Hi stylers

Thank you for a very useful package. I think I have found 1 or perhaps 2 bugs:

- It appears that `style_text()` ignores custom style unless cache is disabled.
- It appears that `style_file()`  w/o cache has unintended side effects such that it can only work once with a custom style. To work again the session must be restarted

``` r
# Prepare transformers
rpolars_style = function() {

  # derive from tidyverse
  transformers = styler::tidyverse_style()

  # reverse tranformer to make <- into =
  transformers$token$force_assignment_op = function (pd) {
    to_replace = pd$token == "LEFT_ASSIGN"
    pd$token[to_replace] = "EQ_ASSIGN"
    pd$text[to_replace] = "="
    pd
  }

  transformers
}


# CACHE does not take into account transformers
styler::style_text("foo <- 42; bar = TRUE", transformers = rpolars_style()) # good
#> foo = 42
#> bar = TRUE
styler::style_text("foo <- 42; bar = TRUE", transformers = styler::tidyverse_style()) # bad
#> foo <- 42
#> bar = TRUE
styler::style_text("foo <- 42; bar = TRUE", transformers = rpolars_style()) # bad
#> foo <- 42
#> bar = TRUE

styler::cache_clear(ask = FALSE)
styler::cache_deactivate()
#> Deactivated cache.
styler::style_text("foo <- 42; bar = TRUE", transformers = rpolars_style()) # good
#> foo = 42
#> bar = TRUE

title: Style `test_that()` calls to make them more BDD/readability-friendly?
description:
## Preamble

The `{testthat}` tests read like sentences (à la BDD), and when the description is in the same line as the function name, this can really boost its readability. For example, the following:

```r
test_that("multiplication works", {
   expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
})
```

can be read mentally as 

> "test that multiplication works as expected"

and the formatting helps this mental dialogue.

## Actual vs Expected

But when the code is styled differently (e.g. using Allman-style indentation), 

``` r
library(styler)

'test_that(
  "multiplication works",
  {
    expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
  }
)' -> code

style_text(code)
#> test_that(
#>   "multiplication works",
#>   {
#>     expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
#>   }
#> )
```

`{styler}` doesn't restyle it to its more readable version:

```r
#> test_that("multiplication works", {
#>   expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
#> })
```

Do you think `{styler}` should by default restyle such calls? Or doing so violates its "non-invasive" nature?

FWIW, the style guide doesn't seem to have anything to say in this matter ([except indirectly](https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html?q=test_tha#indenting)).

## Exception

This is feature request is relevant only when there are no keyword arguments, only positional arguments, are present in the `test_that()` call.

```r
'test_that(
  desc = "multiplication works",
  code = {
    expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
  }
)' -> code

style_text(code)
#> test_that(
#>   desc = "multiplication works",
#>   code = {
#>     expect_equal(2 * 2, 4)
#>   }
#> )
```

title: [Testing] Poor parallelism of test-roxygen-examples-complete.R
description:
I think this file would best be split up into many files to support parallelism. As it stands, this test (`test_that("analogous to test-roxygen-examples-complete")`) takes 5x longer than any other `test_that()` units in the suite.

That means the shard stuck with this test is going to take much longer than all the others.

Ideally, each of these:

```
expect_warning(test_collection(
  "roxygen-examples-complete", "^1[^1234567890]",
  transformer = style_text
), NA)
```

would be in a separate file. I'm not sure the easiest way to accomplish this from an ongoing maintenance PoV.

NB: using different `test_that()` for each won't help since testthat parallelizes _by file_:

https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/parallel.html

title: Double indentation should be an opt-in/out rule
description:
Styler "recently" enforces a rule that double indent function declaration.
Let's say you have the following.

```r
f <- function(
  x,
  y
) {
  "content"
}
```

It will be "messed up" (sorry, personal opinion on double indentation) as:

```r
f <- function(
    x,
    y) {
  "content"
}
```

I know there is #1137 open for few months now, but regardless of this PR, I do believe double indent rule should be as other rules an opt-in/out rule.

Thanks for considering this.

title: Style `test_that()` calls to always contain code in braced expressions?
description:
## Preamble

In recent updates to `{testthat}`, it generates a warning if code is not in a braced expression:

``` r
library(testthat)
local_edition(3L)
test_that("testthat works", expect_equal(1, 1))
#> Warning: The `code` argument to `test_that()` must be a braced expression to
#> get accurate file-line information for failures.
#> Test passed
```

<sup>Created on 2023-11-07 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

But this is not something currently enforced by `{styler}`, and I am wondering if this is something it ought to support?

## Actual output

``` r
styler::style_text('test_that("testthat works", expect_equal(1, 1))')
#> test_that("testthat works", expect_equal(1, 1))
```

<sup>Created on 2023-11-07 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

## Expected output

``` r
styler::style_text('test_that("testthat works", expect_equal(1, 1))')
#> test_that("testthat works", {
#>   expect_equal(1, 1)
#> })
```

title: standalone files imported from other packages should be ignored in `style_pkg()`
description:
Hi,

I think that standalone files from core tidyverse packages should be ignored from styling.
At the moment, the default values for `exclude_files` is `c("R/RcppExports.R", "R/cpp11.R")`, but I think it could be `c("R/RcppExports.R", "R/cpp11.R", "R/import-standalone-*")`

or a new argument
`exclude_import_standalone` that would default to `TRUE`.

If you are not familiar with the new standalone files, here are some references

https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/use_standalone.html

https://github.com/r-lib/rlang/blob/main/R/standalone-types-check.R

A PR in dplyr where they use it tidyverse/dplyr#6722. They also use it in ggplot2

In a package, if I use

```r 
usethis::use_standalone("r-lib/rlang", "types-check")
The file will be copied to `mypkg/R/important-standalone-type-check.R`
# it will be read-only.
# but when I run, `styler::style_pkg()`, it will restyle the file.
```

I think that because these files appear as read-only in RStudio. If they are to be styled, they should be styled in the original repos (in this case in rlang)

which comes down to the `TMPDIR` environment variable being undefined in my setup.  That is annoying.
But this code https://github.com/r-lib/styler/blob/aeaa1faef2e5ea11be26817d8cfa3774ad9d66e7/R/zzz.R#L41 has some problems:
- the result of the second `Sys.getenv()` call is bound to the `winslash` argument of `normalizePath()`, and never evaluated as a potential path (notice three warnings for `path[1]` above).
- `tempdir()` also checks the `TEMP` environment variable, which should be a viable option here too
- `normalizePath()` warns on any of the supplied paths not existing, so for any of the tested variables being unset.

title: Set off each comment with one blank line?
description:
## Preamble

An effective way to get an overview of the code is to read the comments _without_ reading the code. Setting comments off with a blank line helps distinguish code from comments and makes it easy for the reader to scan the code or the comment.

## Actual

This is a minimal reprex to illustrate the issue, but you can scale this to more complex comments and highly involved code block below each comment.

``` r
styler::style_text("# comment-1
if (TRUE) {
  # comment-2
  x <- 1
  # comment-3
  a <- 3
}
# comment-4
x + 1")
#> # comment-1
#> if (TRUE) {
#>   # comment-2
#>   x <- 1
#>   # comment-3
#>   a <- 3
#> }
#> # comment-4
#> x + 1
```

<sup>Created on 2022-11-30 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

## Expected

Note that this doesn't apply to the comments at the start of the scope.

``` diff
#> # comment-1
#> if (TRUE) {
#>   # comment-2
#>   x <- 1
+ #>               
#>   # comment-3
#>   a <- 3
#> }
+ #>               
#> # comment-4
#> x + 1
```

title: Include no or only one blank line between the in-body syntax and code in R knitr chunks
description:
## Description

Having a single blank line between the chunk options and the chunk code helps visually distinguish them. But having more than one blank line is (IMO) rarely desirable. It would be good if `{styler}` could do this.

As for when there is no blank line, I am not sure if we should introduce one because the user intent is more likely to not have any separation between the options and the code.

This issue applies equally to `.Rmd`/`.qmd` docs.

# Example-1

1 blank line

## before

````md
```{r}
#| label = "my_chunk",
#| fig.height = 6,




# code
x <- 1 
```

````

## after

````md
```{r}
#| label = "my_chunk",
#| fig.height = 6,

# code
x <- 1 
```

````

# Example-2

0 blank lines (unsure, but my current preference)

## before

````md
```{r}
#| label = "my_chunk",
#| fig.height = 6,
# code
x <- 1 
```

````

## after

````md
```{r}
#| label = "my_chunk",
#| fig.height = 6,
# code
x <- 1 
```

````

title: Release for rlang 1.1.0 deprecation tweaks?
description:
On the current tip of main (8e9ac82), the styler check performs much better, in terms of memory usage and runtime, than the latest styler release (see r-lib/rlang#1626).  The removal of deprecation warnings by 99d502fc (Replace usage of deprecated rlang::with_handlers(), 2023-04-01, #1103) looks to be a large part of that.

I'm not sure how much any of this is relevant for regular usage (versus a test setting, where code paths are being hit repeatedly), but, even based on the check performance alone, it seems like it might be worth cutting a new styler version.  Are there plans to release soon?

(Thanks for maintaining styler.)

title: styling `dplyr::case_when()`
description:
Reference: #714, i.e. should be one condition per line. Also note overlap with #258 for `~`. 


Unfortunately, the structure of the parse table in `c(x~y)` is not equivalent to `c(x = y)` so we can't rely on the alignment detection algorithm as is 🤔 

``` r
styler::cache_deactivate()
#> Deactivated cache.
styler:::create_tree(
  "c(x = y) ;c(x~y)"
)
#>                                                  levelName
#> 1  ROOT (token: short_text [lag_newlines/spaces] {pos_id})
#> 2   ¦--expr: c(x = [0/1] {1}                              
#> 3   ¦   ¦--expr: c [0/0] {3}                              
#> 4   ¦   ¦   °--SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL: c [0/0] {2}          
#> 5   ¦   ¦--'(': ( [0/0] {4}                               
#> 6   ¦   ¦--SYMBOL_SUB: x [0/1] {5}                        
#> 7   ¦   ¦--EQ_SUB: = [0/1] {6}                            
#> 8   ¦   ¦--expr: y [0/0] {8}                              
#> 9   ¦   ¦   °--SYMBOL: y [0/0] {7}                        
#> 10  ¦   °--')': ) [0/0] {9}                               
#> 11  ¦--';': ; [0/0] {10}                                  
#> 12  °--expr: c(x~y [0/0] {11}                             
#> 13      ¦--expr: c [0/0] {13}                             
#> 14      ¦   °--SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL: c [0/0] {12}         
#> 15      ¦--'(': ( [0/0] {14}                              
#> 16      ¦--expr: x~y [0/0] {15}                           
#> 17      ¦   ¦--expr: x [0/0] {17}                         
#> 18      ¦   ¦   °--SYMBOL: x [0/0] {16}                   
#> 19      ¦   ¦--'~': ~ [0/0] {18}                          
#> 20      ¦   °--expr: y [0/0] {20}                         
#> 21      ¦       °--SYMBOL: y [0/0] {19}                   
#> 22      °--')': ) [0/0] {21}
```

<sup>Created on 2021-02-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0)</sup>

i.e. when at the nest `expr / ~ / exp`, is_alined is false because that's one level up. Without these two being on the same level, a comparison is very hard. We potentially have to move these expressions one level up with `flatten_operators_one()`, but potentially only within function calls. This probably implies `is_tilde_expr()` has to be re-thought too as it is not guaranteed that `~` has position 2 or 3.

title: [Testing] Poor parallelism of test-public_api.R
description:
Much like #1105, we can improve the performance of the styler suite by reducing imbalance across test shards (i.e. files).

No individual `test_that()` unit is as slow as that in #1105, but taken as a whole, test-public_api.R takes much longer than any other file.

The proposed solution here is simpler -- subdivide test-public_api.R into a few files, e.g. test-public_api-{0,1,2}.R, or subdivide by functionality.

Happy to help filing a PR based on the desired subdivision.

I understand that such empty lines should not exist in a package, but running `styler` regularly while actively working on a function led to this issue, which took some time to troubleshoot.

title: New double-indented function style gets undone, causing lint
Understand where styler spends most of the time
description:
This is crucial for #558.

Because we use mostly recursive calls, and effectively each function can call each other function, I suspect it is difficult to see where exactly styler spends most of its time, and which parts perhaps should be optimized. Can you confirm that?

To work around, I propose processing the `.Rprof` files created from a profiler run. If we erase the right places from the call stack for each sample, we might just end up with a clean flat structure that immediately shows where the time is spent. What do you think?

Alternatively, we could (temporarily) replace the recursive calls with `later::later()` or replace recursion with a queue and a `while {}` loop. Editing the call stack sounds like less work.

title: Styling resulted in code that isn't parsable.
When Roxygen comment block ends with a tag, the stylerignore directives are ignored
description:
This was difficult to track down, but I finally have a minimal reprex to show the issue.

----

When the Roxygen comment ends with a tag (any tag), the stylerignore directives are ignored. 

For example, here the Roxygen comment block is surrounded by the stylerignore directives, and yet the code in examples is styled. 

``` r
styler::style_text(
  "# styler: off
#' @examples 
#' x=1
#' @export
# styler: on"
)
#> # styler: off
#> #' @examples
#> #' x <- 1
#> #' @export
#> # styler: on
``` 

And I think that this has something to do with the tag at the end, because if you relocate it to any other position in the comment block, we get the expected behaviour.

``` r
styler::style_text(
  "# styler: off
#' @export
#' @examples 
#' x=1
# styler: on"
)
#> # styler: off
#> #' @export
#> #' @examples 
#> #' x=1
#> # styler: on
```

title: Allowing function-call-style function definitions (argument wrapping in signature)
description:
Consider the following:

```
poisson_gamma_mixture_extended_truncated_metric <- function(predictor_1,
                                                            predictor_2,
                                                            max_valid_value = 100) {
  # ...
}
```

`styler` is happy with this as is but the 3rd line is >80 characters.

My preferred approach to writing a function definition like this is:

```
poisson_gamma_mixture_extended_truncated_metric <- function(
  predictor_1,
  predictor_2,
  max_valid_value = 100
) {
  # ...
}
```

But `styler::style_file()` reverts this usage to the first one.

The compromise that makes styler happy and allows the function to fit within 80 chars is:

```
poisson_gamma_mixture_extended_truncated_metric <-
  function(predictor_1,
           predictor_2,
           max_valid_value = 100) {
    # ...
  }
```

But there are a few issues with this:

 1. Long lines in the function (79 or 80 characters) will be bumped to >80
 2. By bumping the indent level it makes it look like the function is defined on a different level of execution than it is
 3. For changing existing definitions, the diff on version control will look a lot bigger unless whitespace diffs are turned off (usually not by default)

Would it be OK for styler to leave definitions like the "preferred" one alone?

The style guide AFAICT is moot on this particular point. The closest we get is here: https://style.tidyverse.org/functions.html#long-lines-1

```
# Bad
long_function_name <- function(a = "a long argument",
  b = "another argument",
  c = "another long argument") {
  # Here it's hard to spot where the definition ends and the
  # code begins
}
```

My preferred usage I think makes clear the delineation between the signature and the function body by using `) {` on its own separate line.

The style guide _does_ recommend against such long function names as in my original example, but even with "more stylistic" function names this issue has arisen many times on our internal code.

Also filed https://github.com/tidyverse/style/issues/173 to the style guide upstream.

title: Named arguments not forced to one per line?
description:
I had expected 

```R
new("Period", x@.Data[i],
  year = x@year[i], month = x@month[i],
  day = x@day[i], hour = x@hour[i], minute = x@minute[i]
)
```

to be restyled to 

```R
new("Period", x@.Data[i],
  year = x@year[i], 
  month = x@month[i],
  day = x@day[i], 
  hour = x@hour[i],
  minute = x@minute[i]
)
```

Since https://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#long-lines says "use one line each for the function name, each argument, and the closing )".

This rule should only apply to named arguments, and I'd expect the following code to be left as is:

```R
show <- paste(
  x@year, "y ", x@month, "m ", x@day, "d ",
  x@hour, "H ", x@minute, "M ", x@.Data, "S",
  sep = ""
)
```

(I'm spotting these cases because I've started restyling lubridate, which has a mismash of code styles from years of development. styler has made a big improvement and I really appreciate all the work you have put in this package 😄)

title: Indention with multiple tokens starting (but not ending) on same line
description:
Multiple tokens that cause indention on the same line with at least one token causing indention over more than one line are problematic if the unindention they cause is not on the same line. This is because some lines might not be indented at all which looks odd in practice.

``` r
text <- c(
  "a <- 3",
  "b <- 5",
  "c <- purrr::map(a|",
  "b,",
  "a = 1,",
  "c = 2",
  ")"
)
styler::style_text(text)
#> a <- 3
#> b <- 5
#> c <- purrr::map(a |
#>   b,
#> a = 1,
#> c = 2
#> )
```

<sup>Created on 2019-03-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

In the example above, the opening brace does not cause indention because `|` will. But the scope of the indention of `|` ends on the next line, leaving the remainder unindented, although it is within an expression that needs indention. 

Easy fix: Don't allow multiple indention tokens on the same line if their indention scope does not end on the same line but then break the line.
```r
purrr::map(
  a | 
    b, 
  a = 1, 
  c = 2
)
```
The same with braces, i.e. the following is not nice:
```r
{{
  x
}
}
```
But the easy fix is to move the second `{` one line down. Similar to #428, but just that this issue also covers indention of tokens other than braces, but when you look at the examples in #428, I think it becomes evident that the brace case is much more common. This issue is probably also blocked by #357.

description:
These are probably candidates for release 2.0:

* remove `save_after_styling` env variable. Already deprecated.

title: Alignment detection does not factor in how other styling rules change alignment
description:

```r

  1212, 232, f(n= 2),

)
```
Seems aligned on commas, but then later, a space is added after `n` and the result of styling is 
```r
gle(
  1212, 232, f(n = 2),
  1,      2,  "Flar"
)
```
Which is written to the cache (if the cache is active). However, now, the code is not aligned anymore and should therefore be styled like

gle(
  1212, 232, f(n = 2),
  1, 2, "Flar"
)

title: Remove empty lines between roxygen docs and code?
description:
AFAIK, there are currently no guidelines about this in the _tidyverse style guide_, but I was wondering if {styler} should adopt a convention to remove empty lines between roxygen documentation and the code.

- **Actual**

In the wild, I often come across codebases that have formatting like the following. The _count_ of empty spurious lines may differ across files. Currently, {styler} preserves such empty lines.

``` r
styler::style_text(
  "#' @export
  


  foo <- function() NULL"
)
#> #' @export
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> foo <- function() NULL
```

- **Expected new behavior**

I wish {styler} could remove such inconsistencies and adopt a single rule. I'd propose that it removes all empty lines by default, but I am also open to other rules (e.g. always have a single empty line). The point is more about consistency in formatting.

```r
#> #' @export
#> foo <- function() NULL
``` 

- **Exception**

Just like in formatting `R6` lists, I think one exception to this rule could be the presence of a comment block before the function. In such cases, a single empty line can be preserved.

``` r
styler::style_text(
  "#' @export
  
  # bla bla bla
  foo <- function() NULL"
)
#> #' @export
#> 
#> # bla bla bla
#> foo <- function() NULL
```

Curious to hear what you think.

title: Feature: Add option to not detect alignment
description:
An option to not detect alignment would be useful. I think disallowing alignment in code style guides is fairly prevalent. PEP 8 advises against it. The [top stackoverflow result](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/101958/code-formatting-is-lining-up-similar-lines-ok) for the question has split answers, with the top-voted answer advocating strongly against it.

For me personally, the reasons I'd like the styler I use to not allow alignment in code are

- Alignment can't be done *by* styler, only ignored. So if someone aligns one call then it is in a different style than the rest of the code after styling, unless I've somehow convinced everyone on the project to manually align all their code. I'd prefer there to be no red-flag "oh I guess Bob wrote this" signs in the codebase post-styling.
- It requires reviewers of a pull request to review more than they need to. It messes up the commit history / merges / git blame

More on point two in case it isn't obvious what's meant:

Say I'm working on a project and need to add some arguments to this function call. The person who wrote it ran styler, and it was left as-is because it recognized the alignment.

```r
call(
  x = 1,           p = 3,
  y = "something", z = 9
)
```

Ok, so now I add my arguments

```r
call(
  x = 1,           p = 3,
  y = "something", z = 9,
  areallylongarg = 4, extra_arg = 44,
)
```

That doesn't look right, let me use styler...

```r
call(
  x = 1, p = 3,
  y = "something", z = 9,
  areallylongarg = 4, extra_arg = 44,
)
```

After styling the selection line 2 is changed, even though it wasn't part of my code edit. If I submit a pull request, the reviewer will have to read line 2 to make sure I didn't break anything, rather than simply looking at the single line I added. (Ok two lines isn't much but you can imagine cases where there'd be more)

title: Wrong brace indent for not default indent value
description:
There is a case with wrong formatting of curl braces when styler is run with not default indent (`indent_by = 4`).
Here is an example:
```
styler_result <- styler::style_text("
value <- 5
if (value > 0)
    print(value)
",
indent_by = 4
)

print(styler_result)
#> # The result looks like:
#> value <- 5
#> if (value > 0) {
#>       print(value)
#>   }

#> # What I expect to get:
#> value <- 5
#> if (value > 0) {
#>     print(value)
#> }
```

```
styler::style_text(

    indent_by = 4
)
#> value <- 5
#> if (value > 0) {
#>       print(value)
#>   }
```
At the same moment, the example works fine with the default indent (`indent_by = 2`):

```
styler::style_text("

if (value > 0)
    print(value)
")
#> value <- 5
#> if (value > 0) {
#>   print(value)
#> }
```

title: Always have a single space surrounding argument specification?
description:
# observed 

Here I am deliberately adding a single, double, or triple spaces surrounding the argument assignment (`=`), but, when styled, `{styler}` preserves these spaces.

``` r
styler::style_text(
  'df <- dplyr::rename(df,
  "xValues" =   "Time",
  "xUnit" = "TimeUnit",
  "yValues"   = "simulationValues",
  "yUnit" = "unit",
  "yDimension"  = "dimension"
)'
)
#> df <- dplyr::rename(df,
#>   "xValues" =   "Time",
#>   "xUnit" = "TimeUnit",
#>   "yValues"   = "simulationValues",
#>   "yUnit" = "unit",

#> )
```

<sup>Created on 2021-12-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

  "yValues" = "simulationValues",
  "yUnit" = "unit",

title: Feature requests for styling list of functions and arguments
description:
I see at least two ways that this can be improved:

- Deliberately left empty lines between methods and arguments should not be removed. Although the current is minimal, a typical R6 class can be large and with many methods, and it is really helpful to have empty lines to demarcate different functions. [Here is a good example](https://github.com/r-lib/processx/blob/main/R/process.R).  
- Alignment is not detected in "other object properties" part of the class.

``` r
styler::style_text(
"
xData <- R6::R6Class(
  classname = 'xData',
  
  # public fields and methods ------------------------------------
  
  public = list(
    
    initialize = function() {
    },
    
    addx = function(x) {
      private$.x <- x
    },
    
    toDataFrame = function() {
      return(as.data.frame(private$.x))
    }
  ),
  
  # private fields and methods -----------------------------------
  
  private = list(
    .x = NULL,
    .y = NULL
  ),
  
  # other object properties --------------------------------------
  
  lock_objects = TRUE,
  lock_class   = FALSE,
  cloneable    = TRUE,
  portable     = TRUE
)
"
)
#> 
#> xData <- R6::R6Class(
#>   classname = "xData",
#> 
#>   # public fields and methods ------------------------------------
#> 
#>   public = list(
#>     initialize = function() {
#>     },

#>       private$.x <- x
#>     },

#>       return(as.data.frame(private$.x))
#>     }

#>     .x = NULL,

#>   ),
#>

#>

#>   lock_class = FALSE,
#>   cloneable = TRUE,
#>   portable = TRUE
#> )
```

title: Style only part of file that was changed?
description:
I was wondering whether it would be possible to implement a styler function that looks at the dif between the current buffer and the last  saved version and that then only styles those parts that were changed?

I am not sure how hard it is for styler to "know" what has to be styled such that styling the whole buffer is equivalent to styling only the selection but I can imagine it yielding a considerable increase in speed.

title: removing non-roxygen empty lines in docs
description:
If there is an empty line in `{roxygen2}` docs, `{styler}` will leave it be, which makes sense:

``` r
styler::style_text("
                   #' @rdname ggplot2-ggproto
                   #' @import ggplot2
#'
#' @keywords internal
                   ")
#> 
#> #' @rdname ggplot2-ggproto
#> #' @import ggplot2
#> #'
#> #' @keywords internal
```

But do you think it should remove an empty line inserted in the middle of docs?

```r
styler::style_text("
                   #' @rdname ggplot2-ggproto
#' @usage NULL

#' @keywords internal
                   ")
#> 
#> #' @rdname ggplot2-ggproto
#> #' @usage NULL
#> 
#> #' @keywords internal
```

<sup>Created on 2021-11-07 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

I think it should since it is rarely intended that there be an empty non-docs line right in the middle of the documentation.

title: Allow user to opt out of cache removal for current version
description: As introduced with {styler} 1.6.2. `.onLoad()` removes caches for old {styler} versions and all cache files older than 6 days under`R.cache::getCachePath("styler")`, e.g. `"~/Library/Caches/org.R-project.R/R/R.cache/styler"` on my machine. If the user can set another cache root (say `"~/Library/Caches/org.R-project.R/R/R.cache/styler-persistent"`) via an R option, he would opt out of the cache removal. The alternative where the user sets an R option to use the default cache location but not remove older caches has the disadvantage that the startup process must ensure this option. If it does not, e.g. because there is a directory specific `.Rprofile` and the option was previously set in the users home directory `.Rprofile`, the cache is deleted upon {styler} invocation (and restoring it would be possible by moving it to a temp directory but that's annoying). {precommit} could use this cache location by default.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: 'newlines'.
#> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: 'indent'.
#> Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "indent", value = integer(0)): replacement has 0 rows, data has 1
```

<sup>Created on 2018-10-14 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1.9000)</sup>

This works if we add a "minimal style" as extra information, derived from the `initialize` step of `tidyverse_style()` .

``` r
library(styler)
string <- "x <- 'ü'"

style_guide <- list(
  token = list(
    frobnicate = identity
  )
)

minimal_style <- list(
  initialize = tidyverse_style()$initialize,
  use_raw_indention = FALSE,
  reindention = list(comments_only = FALSE)
)

# Why is this necessary?
style_guide <- modifyList(style_guide, minimal_style)

style_text(text = string, transformers = style_guide)
#> x <- 'ü'
```

<sup>Created on 2018-10-14 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

Seems like we could get rid of this requirement by using `isTRUE()` for testing logicals, and by moving the `initialize` step out of `tidyverse_style()`, perhaps hard-code it in _styler_ . What do you think?

title: Multiline `@examplesIf`?
description:
I'm noticing that long lines with the roxygen2 tag `@examplesIf` [get line wrapped with styler](https://github.com/r-lib/styler/blob/e7562f14801bb3886757913911fd54a0e674a80f/tests/testthat/roxygen-examples-complete/23-exampleIf-multiline-cond-out.R#L4-L7). Though my experience has been that roxygen2 doesn't actually support these right now (I've created https://github.com/r-lib/roxygen2/issues/1242 asking about adding that support).

If roxygen2 ends up supporting multi-line `@examplesIf` blocks, styler's current behavior is fine, but currently there appears to be a mismatch.

On another note: I've experienced some oddities when marking these lines as don't style / don't lint. If I do the following:

```
# nolint start
#' @examplesIf long_condition_line
# nolint end
```

And then style the file, the line `# nolint end` is deleted by styler.

If I do the following, everything is fine and the `#' # nolint end` file at the end is not removed:

```
# nolint start
#' @examplesIf long_condition_line
#' # nolint end
```

but that looks a bit funny to my eyes.

title: styler bumps #nolint comments in pipes to the next line

```

  left_join(c, by = c("d" = "e")) %>% # nolint

3: make_transformer(transformers, include_roxygen_examples, base_indention)
4: transform_files(path, transformers = transformers, include_roxygen_examples = include_roxygen_examples, 
5: (function (path, ..., style = tidyverse_style, transformers = style(...),

```

Since {styler.mlr} depends on {styler} HEAD, was there maybe a recent change which might have caused this?

description:
Compare the following:

title: Unwrapping multiple assignments -- intended change?
description:
Some time between v1.3.2 and v1.4.0, `styler` started inlining multiple assignments:

```
# @ v1.3.2
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = '.R')
writeLines('a <-
  b <- 2', tmp)
styler::style_file(tmp)
system(paste('cat', tmp))
# a <-
#   b <- 2
```

```
# @ v1.4.0
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = '.R')
writeLines('a <-
  b <- 2', tmp)
styler::style_file(tmp)
system(paste('cat', tmp))
# a <- b <- 2
```

Is this change intended?

I don't see anything about it in the [release notes](https://github.com/r-lib/styler/releases); only this looks related:

> empty lines are now removed between pipes and assignments (#645, #710).

This behavior is also not described in the tidyverse guide, as near as I can tell.

My attempt to `git bisect` when the change showed up was not successful 😄

styler overwrites changes in an unsaved open file
description:
If you make changes to an open document in RStudio, don't save them and then run `styler::style_dir` or `styler::style_file`, if it makes any changes it will do this on the saved version (rather than the open version) and then overwrite.

I think the ideal fix would be to make changes in an open document if it has unsaved changes. If that's not possible it would be good for styler to throw an error e.g. "Error: Tried to style a document with unsaved changes, please save or close the document then run style_file()" again.

title: Disable styler for knitr R code chunk
description:
It would be nice to be able to disable styler for a particular R chunk in R Markdown documents without including `# styler: off` in the R code chunk.

Instead of this:

````markdown
```{r}
# styler: off
don_t_style_me <- c(____)
# styler: on
```
````

styler could be disabled with the [`tidy` chunk option](https://yihui.org/knitr/options/#code-decoration):


````markdown
```{r tidy=FALSE}
don_t_style_me <- c(____)
```
````

I'd recommend only disabling styler for the chunk if `tidy=FALSE`.

title: `multi_line` attribute could carry amount of line breaks instead of just boolean
description: This should not be harder or more expensive to compute, but gives more context for functions which need to know the number of line breaks in the parse table. It will save time computing them anew multiple times. Currently, a few transformers rely on it but since very expensive, they usually just go one level deep. An application would be https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/371.

title: Allowing line break transformers to depend on multi-line attribute
description:
Line break rules may depend on the structure of the parse table. So we may want to keep curly-brace-expressions as one-liner if the input was one line:
```r
if (x) { x + (1+1) }
```
Note that this is not easily possible. The `multi-line` attribute is not up-to-date for the line break transformers, hence we cannot rely on it. Further, we cannot rely on `line1` and `line2`, because this attribute was removed for safety beforehand (as it's also not up to date). We can try to "pre-reconstruct" the `multi-line` attribute by looking into the children, but that's brittle. One way out would be to split the line break transformers into two groups. One not depending on an up-to-date `multi-line` attribute and one dependent on it. 
We could first apply the first transformer group, then update the `multi-line` attribute and then apply all transformers, updating the `multi-line` attribute between every transformer (which seems expensive).

title: Style syntactically invalid files
description:
lintr has infrastructure for extracting partial parse data from invalid source files, we could borrow that.

1. Create a `srcfile()`: https://github.com/jimhester/lintr/blob/e926089a0187aac01ce6981a798c5dc22e3a4273/R/get_source_expressions.R#L7
2. Use `tryCatch()` with `parse()` and this `srcfile`, this populates the parse data which then can be extracted:  https://github.com/jimhester/lintr/blob/e926089a0187aac01ce6981a798c5dc22e3a4273/R/get_source_expressions.R#L80

See examples in [`?parse`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.4.3/topics/parse).

title: Custom style-guide for semicolons
description:
Hi, my workplace requires semicolons at the end of statements in R.

I used https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/oneliner and came up with this:

```
library("styler")
library("tidyverse")
cache_deactivate()

add_semi_colon <- function(pd_nested) {
    needs_semicolon <- which(
                        # pd_nested$newlines == 1 & pd_nested$token == "expr"
                        styler:::lag(pd_nested$newlines == 1 & pd_nested$token == "expr")
    )
    create_token <- function(pos) {
      semicolumn_pds <- styler:::create_tokens(
        "';'", ";",
        pos_ids = pos)
      return(semicolumn_pds)
    }
    positions <- map_dbl(needs_semicolon, styler:::create_pos_ids, pd = pd_nested)
    for (i in positions) {
      pd_nested <- styler:::bind_rows(pd_nested, create_token(i)) %>%
        styler:::arrange(pos_id)
    }
    return(pd_nested)
  }

semicolon_style <- function() {
  create_style_guide(
    token = lst(add_semi_colon),
    use_raw_indention = TRUE,
    reindention = tidyverse_reindention(),
    style_guide_name = "blab",
    style_guide_version = "v1"
  )
}
```

This almost works, but for lines that look like 

```
p_load(
  tidyverse,
  fs,  # allows reading in multiple files
  RColorBrewer,  # colors
  scales,  # colors
  dendextend,  # allows extraction of data from dendograms
  ggdendro,  # creates ggplot dendrograms
  patchwork,  # allows patching ggplots together
  config
  )
```

It adds to spaces after config and then places the semicolon there: see below.

```
p_load(
  tidyverse,
  fs,  # allows reading in multiple files
  RColorBrewer,  # colors
  scales,  # colors
  dendextend,  # allows extraction of data from dendograms
  ggdendro,  # creates ggplot dendrograms
  patchwork,  # allows patching ggplots together
  config  ;
  )
```

It would be great to have this working, as it would allow me to inter-convert from the tidyverse style to my work's style.

title: Inconsistent behavior of base_indention
description:
Currently, `c("expr", "0")` is used in languageserver to preserve the indention of the cursor for on-type-formatting. We are trying to adopt the newly added `base_indention` in styler 1.4.0 instead of hacking into the stylers (https://github.com/REditorSupport/languageserver/issues/400). However, `base_indention` may produce inconsistent output:

```
> styler::style_text("x+1", base_indention = 2)                                                                                                    
  x + 1

> styler::style_text("x+1\n0", base_indention = 2)                                                                                                 
  x + 1
  0

> styler::style_text(c("x+1", "0"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                            
  x + 1
0

> styler::style_text(c("x+1", "x+2"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                          
  x + 1
  x + 2

> styler::style_text(c("x+1", "f"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                            
  x + 1
  f

> styler::style_text(c("x+1", "1"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                            
  x + 1
  1

> styler::style_text(c("  x+1", "1"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                          
  x + 1
1

> styler::style_text(c("  x+1\n1"), base_indention = 2)                                                                                            
  x + 1
1
```

title: make use of new selection-based API in next release of rstudioapi?
description:
The next version of RStudio will come with support for a visual editing mode, as described in https://rstudio.github.io/visual-markdown-editing/#/. Unfortunately, many of the pre-existing `rstudioapi` APIs are not compatible with visual editing mode, since they assume a line-based editor, where cursor positions can be referenced globally via [row, column] offsets. The new visual editor is cell-based and so does not map to the same abstraction as well.

To help alleviate this, we are introducing a few new APIs that addin authors can use to ensure their addins function both in visual and source mode. Would you be receptive to a PR making that possible?

title: Detect alignment
description:
**UPDATE:** Alignment detection was implemented for function calls: https://styler.r-lib.org/articles/detect-alignment.html

- [x] multiple named arguments in function calls (https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/pull/663#discussion_r146549784)
- [ ] multiple unnamed arguments in single-line function calls (https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/pull/663/commits/0f61d06bf0e3bd382831ffbe6b2bf8f13cff0bbc#diff-3f2ca9f70d2f3617419c503141c9e6fbR6)
- [ ] comments (https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/pull/663#discussion_r146549784)
- [ ] `~` in function calls like `case_when()` and friends.

Rough outline:

- Look at the horizontal position of the corresponding items in the original code
- If the majority is aligned and the alignment involves >1 space somewhere, we store this somewhere in the nested parse data
- When rendering, the alignment is restored

Although it doesn't explicitly recommend that when the function definition looks like the following, there should be one argument per line to improve readability, but I am guessing that this is something implicitly being hinted at? Not sure.

title: The use of scope is not consistent in the API
description:
`create_style_guide()` uses 
* initialize
* line_break
* space
* token
* indention

where `scope` in `tidyverse_style()` can be

* none
* spaces
* indention
* line_breaks
* tokens

Since 99% of users use `tidyverse_style()` to specify a style and not `create_style_guide()`,  I suggest keep the former and adapt the latter, i.e. to deprecate
* line_break -> line_breaks
* space -> spaces
* token -> tokens

An remove the old version in a later release. This includes unifying internals too. In addition, `token` is singular, `tokens` plural, but in our parse data, we use `token` but then also `spaces` and `line_breaks`.

title: Allow specifying AsIs scope without including lower-level transformations
description:
When you select `scope = 'tokens'`, you implicitly choose to select also spaces, indention, line break, i.e. scope is cummulative. See `help(tidyverse_style, package = 'styler')`. For certain applications, you don't want to have lower-level transformations, i.e. for [indenting lines for vscode](https://twitter.com/lorenzwalthert/status/1325864878712754177), you don't want to style spaces. I think we might simply want to use `I()` to indicate non-cummulative scopes. `I()` changes the class to `AsIs` and we can handle this internally. This is a non-breaking API change:
```r
style_text("1+\n1", scope = I("indention")) # to only style indention
style_text("1+\n1", scope = I(c("spaces", "token")) # spaces and token only
style_text("1+\n1", scope = "indention") # spaces and indention
```

Internals probably should be refactored to operate on a factor vector with `scopes` instead of the highest-level scope. Note that this will invalidate the cache as the scope argument will now be represented differently internally.

cc: @renkun-ken.

title: feature request: not changing trailing comment for highlighting in `xaringan`
description:
The trailing comment `#<<` can be used to highlight lines in `xaringan` presentations: https://slides.yihui.org/xaringan/#30

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11330453/100471742-34fe8a80-30db-11eb-8877-5b17236abcca.png)

But `styler` changes `#<<` to `# <<`, which removes the highlighting from slides:

``` r
styler::style_text("foo(
  data = mtcars,
  x = cyl,
  y = wt #<<
)")
#> foo(
#>   data = mtcars,
#>   x = cyl,
#>   y = wt # <<
#> )
```

<sup>Created on 2020-11-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

title: { / } and line breaks in function calls
description:
The tidyverse style guide states in section 2.4 that 

A `}` should always go on its own line, unless it’s followed by `else` or `)`. 

So that's why we implemented `remove_line_break_before_round_closing()` which is responsible for
the line breaks removed in [tikzDevice](https://github.com/yihui/tikzDevice/commit/1e4c965d4b3873966109bfc8b877ae7b8fbdfbeb). 


I personally think that's fine, but we may only include this rule if `strict = TRUE`.

Also it says that  a `{` should never go on its own line and should always be followed by a new line, so 
```r

tryCatch(
{
  ...
} 
```
from the above-referenced commit is in my eyes not compliant with the tidyverse style guide.

title: Tab conversion
description:
Tabs used to be converted to spaces, e.g. 10a3c68b.
```r
make_transformer_nested <- function(transformers) {
  function(text) {
    text <- gsub(" +$", "", text)
    text <- gsub("\t", "        ", text)

    pd_nested <- compute_parse_data_nested(text)
    transformed_pd_nested <- visit(pd_nested, transformers)
    # TODO verify_roundtrip
    new_text <- serialize_parse_data_nested(transformed_pd_nested)
    new_text
  }
}
```
* The tidyverse [style guide](http://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#indenting) does encourage the use of spaces, not tabs.
* We'd principally prefer an approach that operates on the parse table and not on the text input, so third-party style guides could leave tabs untouched.
* There seems another bug in the [parser](https://github.com/jimhester/lintr/blob/aa70430282852afa15a61cc69771e71dd32e1aec/R/get_source_expressions.R#L210) that might be relevant for this.

title: Preventing vertical styling of R expression (bquote)
description:
Is it possible to prevent the styler package to reformat bquote/expression like this one?

```r
bquote(km ~ h^{-1})
```
At the moment, `styler` re-indent it vertically.

![Peek 2020-11-19 09-42](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4519221/99707023-e8c3a280-2a69-11eb-9311-c4ebc92017c2.gif)

It would be nice to be able to specify an option to only re-indent horizontally (i.e. add missing spaces).

For example,

```r
bquote(km~h^{-1})
```
would become (or whatever match the tidyverse rules)

```r
bquote(km ~ h ^ { -1 })
```
I think that would be greatly appreciated for people that use `bquote` or `expression` when making ggplot2 graphics for example.

title: Need a way to preserve initial indention of the input expression
description:
In a code editor, when user performs range formatting, the selected code might have initial indention. The code editor should preserve the indention since the selected code could be part of nested scopes like the following:

No initial indention:

```r
data <- dbQuery(
  con,
  "select name, group, max(update_time) as max_time
     from users
     where date = 20200525
     group by group"
)
```

`data <- dbQuery(...)` has initial indention to be preserved:

```r
fun <- function(x, y) {
  data <- dbQuery(
    con,
    "select name, group, max(update_time) as max_time
     from users
     where date = 20200525
     group by group"
  )
}
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4662568/82775638-e0076080-9e7a-11ea-923a-9f636b041835.png)

Calling `styler::style_text()` on text with initial indention removes it.

I'm wondering if there's a simple way to preserve the initial indention of the input code?

Related to https://github.com/REditorSupport/languageserver/issues/264.

description:
We should test it and check the magnitude of speed gains, as this is a feature of the release according to a [blog post](https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2020/08/magrittr-2-0/).

```r
x <- purrr::rerun(20, bench::system_time(styler::style_file("R/roxygen-examples-add-remove.R")))

# release: 1.463225

#> 0.08
```

A quick speed test shows that we'll gain about 8% in speed. We should require `magrittr >= 2.0` once available.

title: Improve benchmarking infra
description:
* The variance in the timing estimates are probably > 1%. A PR and a base reference where no effect on speed is expected (because no such code was touched, #631), gave a ~2% difference.
* add time-line plot.
* artifact should have name of branch when uploaded to later easily compare different artifact.
* absolute median timing should be posted in PR for easy reference.
* Need an easy way to show median is x% worse or better than base branch. Currently, we need to estimate from hand and first guess the median. Could be in the plot or posted as comment.
* Need additional benchmark. Now we have without cache and with cache. The usefulness of `with_cache` is limited because it is so close to 0 (since it's always full text cached already). We don't have with cache activated and empty cache. This would be helpful for understanding the impact of #679 for example, or any improvement that relates to the cache. The interpretation of it would include the time required for `git reset` and can hence not be taken as absolute time to style code, but only in comparison with the base branch (where `git reset` also occurs).

title: Changing styling options has no effect unless file is changed
description:
This is a bit minor, but essentially: after running `style_*(<some file etc>)`, then running it again with a new style, e.g. `style_*(<some file etc>, transformers = tidyverse_style(indent_by = 4))` nothing will happen. If the file is edited in any way, then the second command will work correctly. 

I believe this is a cache issue, but could be wrong.

The issue is that if you run styler on a file with the wrong settings, every function must be touched by an edit to "break" the cache.

## Example

Say we had an example file `test.R` that only had the following:
```R
test_func <- function(x) {

   x + 2
}
```
(with three spaces before the `x` on the third line)

Then running `style_file("test.R")` will give (as expected):

```R
test_func <- function(x) {
  x + 2
}
```

Now we decide we want four spaces. We should run (I think) `style_file("test.R", transformers = tidyverse_style(indent_by = 4))`, but in this case nothing happens (`✔ 	0	File unchanged.`).

Then, if any edit is made to the file, even a change unrelated to indenting, the above command *does* work and correctly changes the file to:
```R
test_func <- function(x) {
    x + 2
}
```

NOTE: in testing, this "fix" **only worked for the function edited, not the whole file**. So I had to make edits to every function in the desired file to get the correct result.

## Best Guess

I guess this is a rule about the caching: if the function is unchanged after the previous `styler` run, it is reasonable to assume that no styling should be done, but of course this isn't the case if the style rules have changed. 

## Version and System

I got this on the latest CRAN release, 1.3.2. I got the same behaviour (with less testing) on the current dev version on github, `9c5d88328294d0c7a32818550bc99f6526f25b0d`.

MacOS Catalina 10.15.5

## Thanks

Thanks for the package, very useful! My apologies if the above issue is simply just misuse on my part.

title: Bioc-friendly style feature suggestion
description:
Hi,

Based on my recent work for https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/84 and at https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/02_update.R, I want to make a few PR to `styler`.

When you submit a new package to Bioconductor, they run `BiocCheck` as in https://github.com/Bioconductor/Contributions/issues/1393#issuecomment-613458478 which links to http://bioconductor.org/spb_reports/regutools_buildreport_20200414095652.html. `BiocCheck` runs some code style checks and any failures are reported as `NOTE`s, more on this at http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/BiocCheck/inst/doc/BiocCheck.html#formatting-checks. On that paragraph in the vignette they refer readers to `formatR` (also on logs when you get an error). However, `formatR` doesn't work that well as `styler` (I had issues where say `overlaps = "5' prime"` gets re-formatted into `overlaps = ''5 prime'`). There's still the issue about line lengths https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/247 which `BiocCheck` will check, but as noted in the issue thread, even `formatR` can't fix things.

I only discovered `styler` yesterday and saw that it worked fairly well for my `derfinderPlot` package. One difference between the tidyverse style guide https://style.tidyverse.org/ and the Bioconductor style guide http://www.bioconductor.org/developers/how-to/coding-style/ that is easy to address, is the 2 vs 4 space indentation. One that is trickier is the definition of functions with many arguments where the tidyverse style recommends this https://style.tidyverse.org/functions.html#long-lines-1 and the bioc style wants 4 spaces still. 

With the help of a few `print()` statements, I looked at `tidyverse_style()$indentation$update_indentation_ref_fun_dec` and modified it at https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/02_update.R#L2-L12.

```R
bioc_style <- styler::tidyverse_style(indent_by = 4)
bioc_style$indention$update_indention_ref_fun_dec <- function(pd_nested) {
    if (pd_nested$token[1] == "FUNCTION") {
        seq <- rlang::seq2(3, nrow(pd_nested) - 2)
        pd_nested$indention_ref_pos_id[seq] <- pd_nested$pos_id[nrow(pd_nested)]
        pd_nested$indent[seq] <- pd_nested$indent[seq] + 4
    }
    pd_nested
}
```

The idea of the potential PR would be to add a function `bioc_style()` that builds upon `tidyverse_style()` to make `styler` more bioc-friendly. It won't be the full bioc-style, but it'll resemble it a lot more. In the future maybe other things I missed that could be added to this function. The goal would be for have Bioc developers run `styler::style_pkg(transformers = styler::bioc_style() )` after the PR is complete. Hm... maybe `bioc_like_style()` would be a better name so it's clearer that it's not 100% the bioc style.

I'll make a companion issue at `BiocCheck` for updating the recommendation to use `styler` instead of `formatR` (or maybe list both). Though having a `bioc_style()` in `styler` would be a lot more easy to use than telling them about the code in https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/02_update.R#L2-L12 or incorporating it in another package.

Best,
Leo

title: Dry-run mode
description:
Is it possible to run `styler` in dry-run/check-only mode, where it simply reports what would be formatted?

Our use-case for this is to use `styler` in a pre-commit hook on the developer's side, and as part of CI/CD tests once code has been received by git server.

Technically we could solve this by using temporary directories and a lot of copying and diff-ing. However it would be much simpler if `style_dir` accepted parameter `check_only=T` or `dry_run=T`.

We would then use the output of this function inside `stopifnot` for example, such that our scripts will fail, thereby halting the commit or failing the test run.

Python's code formatter `black` has this functionality: by running `black --check`, nothing gets modified and it will exit with non-zero exit code if something would have been formatted. This makes it very easy to use in pre-commit hooks and CI/CD tests.

title: Redundant line breaks in function header not removed when formatting
description:
After resolving #541, `tryCatch` blocks now terminate in a new line.

```
code <- "tryCatch({
  my_options <- options()
  print('hello!')
},
error = function(e) e)
"
styler::style_text(code)
#> tryCatch(
#>   {
#>    my_options <- options()
#>    print("hello!")
#>  },
#>  error = function(e) e
#> )
```

This seems like one good case from #125, but there are examples in that issue where the original formatting was considered correct.

Similarly, function signatures that used a wrapped style for arguments also end in an empty new line.

```
code <- "function(
    my_indendented_arg, and_another) {
  print('hello')
}"
styler::style_text(code)
#> function(
#>          my_indendented_arg, and_another) {
#>   print("hello")
#> }
```

These seem to be related as cases where there are empty new lines after an opening paren.

Thanks!

description: Before introducing caching, there was no need for this, as it would happen automatically. However, the cache does not catch that "1-1" and "1-1 " is essentially the same. Hence, we should remove trailing spaces before processing so the cache is active in this case too.
